group: Message.getOPT() - OPT record retrieval from ADDITIONAL section

cases.expected: OPTRecord instance (the first OPTRecord in the ADDITIONAL section)
cases.description: The ADDITIONAL section contains a single OPTRecord. getOPT() should iterate over the section, detect the instance of OPTRecord and return it.

cases.expected: OPTRecord instance (the first OPTRecord among several records)
cases.description: The ADDITIONAL section contains several records (e.g., ARecord, AAAARecord) followed by an OPTRecord and then other records. getOPT() must return the first encountered OPTRecord, ignoring preceding non‑OPT records.

cases.expected: OPTRecord instance (the first of multiple OPTRecords)
cases.description: The ADDITIONAL section contains two OPTRecord objects (perhaps with different UDP payload sizes). The method should stop at the first one and return it, never reaching the second.
The ADDITIONAL section contains records, but none are instances of OPTRecord. After scanning the whole list, getOPT() should fall through the loop and return null.
The ADDITIONAL section is empty (getSection(Section.ADDITIONAL) returns an empty list). The loop body never executes, and the method returns null.

group: Message.getOPT() - Null entries in ADDITIONAL section

cases.expected: OPTRecord instance (the first non‑null OPTRecord in the ADDITIONAL section)
cases.description: The ADDITIONAL section list contains a leading null element, followed by an OPTRecord and then other records. The method should safely ignore the null, detect the OPTRecord and return it.
The ADDITIONAL section list contains only null elements. The loop should skip all nulls and ultimately return null.
A subclass of Message overrides getSection(int) to return null for the ADDITIONAL section. The for‑each loop in getOPT() attempts to iterate over a null reference, causing a NullPointerException.
A subclass of Message overrides getSection(int) to throw an IllegalStateException when called for the ADDITIONAL section. The exception propagates out of getOPT().

A custom List implementation is returned by getSection(Section.ADDITIONAL) whose iterator throws ConcurrentModificationException on the first call to hasNext(). This simulates a concurrent modification during iteration, which should be propagated by getOPT().
